Alderman BURGESS : If he says he has not been sneak- ing here to make this attack upon me to-night, I will withdraw. Henry Roberts is no sneak—he is not big enough. I" Oh, oh.") Councillor ROBERTS : Mr. Mayor, lam a member of this Council. I am sent here by a section of the rate- payers of Warrington even if I am personally not entitled to respect. That is my position, and I intend that posi- tion to be respected. (Hear, hear.) If Alderman Burgess will not withdraw that word, I shall obstruct the • business of this Corporation till he does. Alderman HARRISON : I think we shall have to pro- ceed against that. , Alderman BURGESS : What have Ito withdraw ? , Councillor DIXON: The word "sneak." , Alderman BURGESS : I have withdrawn it ; I said he ' was too little for that. L The MAYOR : Can you not withdraw it without making . any comment ? Alderman BURGESS : Oh, yes, if it will please Mr. Henry Roberts or anybody else. A vote was then taken when Councillor Flood's amend- was carried by 19 votes to two votes, only Alderman Burgess, and Councillor Hepherd voting against. ' The minutes, as amended, were afterwards passed. L, COUNCILLOR DIXON AND TEE DISCHARGED SCAVENGER. ; Councillor Dixon, pursuant to notice moved" that the full particulars of the discharge of the man Sutton, who was a scavenger, be given to me." The motion was L not seconded, and the proceedings concluded. PAVING AND SEWERAGE COMMITTEE. This Committee recommended that the necessarysteps he taken for the forming and paving of New-road, Latch- ford ; that the tender of Mr. Patrick Finegan to supply 200 tons of setts at 19s. per ton (f.o.b. Liverpool) be ' accepted ; also that the following tenders for the forming , and paving of the foltowinc, streets be accepted : William Heaton, for Morris-yard, Silver-street, £llB 2s. ; William Heaton, Silver Square, £72; Thomas Allen, passage off Pierpoint-street, £l7B 10s. ; Simeon Hough, Pinshop Yard, £129 Bs. 9d. The minutes were confirmed on the motion of Alder- man WRIGHT. MARKETS COMMITTEE. The Committee reported to the total income from all sources for the past four weeks, was £384 9s 5d ; corres- ponding period last year, £396 I7s. Bd. decrease, £l2 Bd. 3d. The minutes also contained a resolution fixing the charge to market auctioneers, at 7s. 6d per day. These minutes were adopted on the motion of the CHAIRMAN, seconded by Councillor BLACKHURST. NEWSPAPERS AT THE LIBRARY. On moving the minutes of the Museum Committee, Councillor H. ROBERTS mentioned that the Library was now provided with newspapers. THE BATHS AND PARK. The RathS, &c., Committe reported that the income for the baths for the past four weeks was £43 155., and for corresponding period last year, £25 6d. 4d., The com- mittee also recommended acceptance of tenders for engineering work it the new baths, and the erection of a band stand in the park, as mentioned in the •• Examiner " last week. Councillor BOLTON moved the adoption, with the ex- ception of the recommendation that Messrs. Bradford's tender be accepted, as the contract had not been adver- tised for. As to the tender of £265 for the new band- stand he explained that the old one was rotten, and the committee thought it was necessary to make a good job of the matter. Alderman WRIGHT seconded the motion, which was adopted. THE CEMETERY. From the report of the Registrar to this Committee it appeared that the interments for the past four weeks were—adults, 38 ; minors, 36 ; stillborn and premature, 12. The receipts for the past four weeks were £55 7s. Bd. ; corresponding period last year, £63 10s. 6d. The minutes. were Cenfirined on the motion of Alder- man HARIIISOL TEE OAS COMMITTEE. This Committee reported to the average illuminating power of gas for the past four weeks, was equal to 1852 weeks candles at both works. They also recom- mended the reduction of meter rents to the scale given in those columns last week. It was recommended that the tender of Messrs. J. and J. Braddock to supply a Gas Governor at £6B 55. Od., and the tender of the Stanton Ironworks, fer tha supply of pipes and special castings, be accepted. Alderman HOLMES moved the adoption of the minutes. He said the amount of money contemplated to be spent on Longford works would be a little over £20,000. The contract amounted to £14,000, and in addition there would be a further estimated expenditure of £6,345, total £20,300, and there was a further outlay required, probably two or three thousands more. Councillor R. T. FAIRCLOUGH seconded. Alderman IlcaziEs in reply to Councillor Shaw-Green, said the Committee did not contemplate increasing the price of gas. They would rather, if anything, be in- clined to reduce it. Councillor SHAW-Gil/EN, seconded and the report was adopted.
